materials.name: PET
materials.description: PET is one of the most widely used food-grade plastics. It offers excellent clarity, good barrier properties against moisture and gases, and is lightweight. Commonly used for bottles, trays, and flexible films.
key_properties: Suitable for carbonated beverages and ready-to-eat foods
not_suitable_for: Products requiring very low oxygen transmission
Extended shelf life beyond 2 years without modification
materials.regulatory: FDA 21 CFR 177.1630 approved. EFSA compliant for food contact.
materials.sustainability_notes: Highly recyclable in most municipal systems. Recycled PET (rPET) reduces carbon footprint by up to 50%. Not biodegradable.
materials.embedding_text: PET polyethylene terephthalate plastic packaging clear transparent moisture barrier oxygen barrier food beverage bottles trays recyclable FDA approved temperature range fresh food snacks beverages

materials.name: HDPE
materials.description: HDPE provides excellent moisture barrier properties and chemical resistance. It is rigid, durable, and suitable for a wide temperature range including freezing and hot-fill applications. Widely used for dairy, juices, and dry food packaging.
materials.sustainability_notes: Widely recycled. Good candidate for post-consumer recycled content. Lower carbon footprint than multi-layer alternatives.
materials.embedding_text: HDPE high density polyethylene plastic packaging moisture barrier dairy milk juice frozen food chemical resistant hot fill wide temperature range recyclable opaque containers

materials.name: LDPE
materials.description: LDPE is a flexible, soft plastic primarily used for films, bags, and flexible packaging. It provides good moisture resistance but poor oxygen barrier. Commonly used as inner liners, produce bags, and flexible pouches.
materials.sustainability_notes: Recyclable but collection infrastructure is limited. Being phased out in many regions due to single-use plastic regulations.
materials.embedding_text: LDPE low density polyethylene flexible plastic film bags produce bread frozen food moisture resistant heat sealable low cost flexible packaging pouches

materials.name: PP
materials.description: Polypropylene offers high heat resistance, making it ideal for hot-fill, microwave-safe, and retort packaging. It provides good moisture barrier and moderate oxygen resistance. Used extensively in yogurt cups, deli containers, and microwavable trays.
materials.regulatory: FDA 21 CFR 177.1520 approved. Microwave-safe grades tested per FDA standards.
materials.sustainability_notes: Recyclable and increasingly collected in curbside programs. High recycled content possible. Lower density means less material per package.
materials.embedding_text: PP polypropylene plastic packaging heat resistant microwave safe hot fill retort yogurt dairy deli containers microwavable trays high temperature moisture barrier recyclable

materials.name: Glass
materials.description: Glass provides an absolute barrier to gases, moisture, and chemicals. It is chemically inert, preserving food flavour and quality indefinitely. Ideal for premium products, acidic foods, and products requiring high-temperature sterilization. Heavy and fragile but infinitely recyclable.
materials.regulatory: Universally approved for food contact. No migration concerns. Compliant with all major food safety regulations.
materials.sustainability_notes: Infinitely recyclable. High energy to produce initially but recycling rates are high. Heavy weight increases transport emissions.
materials.embedding_text: glass packaging absolute barrier oxygen moisture chemically inert premium sterilizable baby food beverages sauces preserves recyclable high temperature food safety no migration

materials.name: Aluminum
materials.description: Aluminum provides total barrier to light, oxygen, moisture, and contaminants. Used extensively in beverage cans, foil pouches, retort pouches, and pharmaceutical packaging. Excellent for long shelf life products and thermally processed foods.
key_properties: Suitable for retort and thermal processing
not_suitable_for: Highly acidic products (corrosion risk without lacquer coating)
materials.regulatory: FDA and EFSA approved. Internal lacquer coatings must be food-grade certified.
materials.sustainability_notes: Aluminum recycling saves 95% of energy compared to virgin production. High recycling rates globally. Infinitely recyclable.
materials.embedding_text: aluminum foil cans total barrier oxygen moisture light barrier retort MAP beverage cans ready meals long shelf life thermally processed pharmaceutical recyclable

materials.name: Paperboard
materials.description: Paperboard is sustainable, printable, and renewable. When coated with polyethylene or barrier coatings, it provides adequate protection for dry goods, cereals, and short shelf-life products. Widely used in folding cartons, Tetra Pak-style cartons, and quick-service restaurant packaging.
key_properties: Poor moisture barrier unless coated (MVTR: 15 g/m²/day)
not_suitable_for: Long shelf life (>6 months) without additional barriers
materials.regulatory: FDA approved for food contact. Inks and coatings must comply with 21 CFR 176.170.
materials.sustainability_notes: Highest sustainability scores among conventional packaging. Renewable source, compostable uncoated grades, widely recycled.
materials.embedding_text: paperboard carton paper packaging dry goods cereals sustainable renewable compostable recyclable printable cereal boxes fast food short shelf life low moisture barrier

materials.name: PLA
materials.description: PLA is a bioplastic derived from renewable resources such as corn starch or sugarcane. It is industrially compostable and offers good clarity similar to PET. Suitable for short shelf life products in ambient or refrigerated conditions. Temperature limited — not suitable for hot products.
key_properties: Good clarity — similar appearance to PET
Not suitable for hot-fill or high-temperature applications
materials.regulatory: FDA approved for food contact. Compostability certified under ASTM D6400 and EN 13432.
materials.sustainability_notes: Industrially compostable. Renewable feedstock. However, industrial composting infrastructure is limited in many regions. Not recyclable in standard streams.
materials.embedding_text: PLA polylactic acid bioplastic compostable bio-based renewable corn starch fresh produce salad containers cold beverages clarity compostable sustainable packaging eco-friendly

materials.name: PHA
materials.description: PHA bioplastics are produced by microbial fermentation and offer superior barrier properties among bioplastics. They are home and industrially compostable, biodegradable in marine environments, and suitable for a wider temperature range than PLA. Premium cost limits widespread adoption.
key_properties: No land competition with food crops (some grades)
applications: Single-use items with high sustainability requirements
not_suitable_for: Applications where recycling is preferred over composting
materials.regulatory: FDA food contact approved. Biodegradability certified per ASTM D5511, ISO 14855.
materials.sustainability_notes: Highest eco-score of all packaging materials. True circular end-of-life. Marine biodegradable. Production carbon footprint still being optimized.
materials.embedding_text: PHA polyhydroxyalkanoates bioplastic biodegradable compostable marine biodegradable home compostable premium sustainable packaging renewable biological fermentation high barrier biobased

materials.name: Multilayer
materials.description: Multilayer packaging combines multiple materials (e.g., PET/foil/PE, EVOH layers, nylon laminates) to achieve properties no single material can provide. Offers exceptional barrier against oxygen, moisture, and light. Widely used for retort pouches, vacuum packaging, and extended shelf life products. Major sustainability challenge due to difficulty of recycling mixed materials.
key_properties: Extended shelf life up to 3+ years
Difficult to recycle — major sustainability challenge
applications: Vacuum packaging for meat and cheese
not_suitable_for: Applications where end-of-life management is critical
materials.regulatory: FDA and EFSA approved. Each layer must individually comply with food contact regulations.
materials.sustainability_notes: Lowest recyclability among all packaging types. Mixed materials cannot be separated economically. Being phased out in EU single-use plastics directives for some applications.
